metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the success metric with the parent: either state the metric as the realized net delta measured on `main` ~a week after filing (per the operator ruling), or explicitly record and justify the narrowing to a pre-filing declared sum plus the post-close shortfall loop as the parent-intended equivalent.
evidence: Parent operator ruling, deliverable 6: 'a success metric measured on `main` a week later rather than by tickets filed'
Leaf AC: 'Its success metric is the summed declared delta of the tickets a run files, computed by the run before filing, and NOT tickets filed.'
Leaf 'The change' bullet: 'the run itself sums those declared deltas before filing ... that sum, not tickets filed, is the run's result'

The leaf's corrective loop ('a closed tidying ticket whose merged diff removed less than it declared records the shortfall') is a post-merge check but is framed as shortfall correction, not as the success metric; the stated success metric remains the pre-filing declared sum
findings.finding: The leaf redefines the janitor's success metric relative to the parent. The parent (operator ruling 2026-11-02, deliverable 6) specifies 'a success metric measured on `main` a week later rather than by tickets filed,' i.e., a post-merge measurement of what actually landed. The leaf instead defines the success metric as 'the summed declared delta of the tickets a run files, computed by the run before filing' (a pre-filing projection). Both agree it is not 'tickets filed,' but they are different quantities: projected pre-filing sum vs. realized delta on main a week later.
findings.location: AC line 'Its success metric is the summed declared delta of the tickets a run files, computed by the run before filing' and 'The change' bullet on the run summing declared deltas before filing
scenarios: A reviewer verifying the leaf against the parent finds the leaf's success metric (pre-filing declaration) does not match the parent's (post-merge measurement on main a week later), leaving it ambiguous whether the parent's intent — judging by what actually landed — is met
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence reconciling the two: keep the pre-filing declared sum as the FILING gate, and name the post-merge measurement on `main` (~1 week later) as the run's SUCCESS metric that feeds the corrective loop — making explicit that the declared sum is a precondition, not the parent's success metric.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how a 'change class' is keyed (e.g. by deletion target/kind recorded on the ticket), where the per-class failure tally comes from (counting closed tidying tickets whose merged diff removed less than declared), and the ==2 suppression rule, in the skill body.
evidence: Plan states the loop 'runs through the tracker the skill already reads for prior decisions' but gives no key by which a 'change class' is identified across tickets, nor how a per-class failure count of two is derived from a set of closed tickets.

The existing prior-decision mechanism (SKILL.md:89-92, Phase-2 prior_decision) matches by code/ticket intent, not by an abstract 'change class' with a ==2 threshold — so the counter has no existing home to inherit.

A 'shortfall' is recorded on a closed ticket, but the plan does not say the per-class tally is a count of such shortfall records vs. a separately persisted counter, leaving the increment site unspecified.
findings.finding: The corrective loop's state increment is ambiguously placed: 'a change class that twice failed to net-reduce is not re-proposed' never defines what a 'change class' is, who counts the two failures, or where that count lives — only that 'the next run reads closed tidying tickets'.
findings.location: The change — 'the corrective loop runs through the tracker ... a closed tidying ticket whose merged diff removed less than it declared records the shortfall, and a change class that twice failed to net-reduce is not re-proposed'; AC 'It names the actor and loop that correct a shortfall'
scenarios: First run has no closed tidying tickets; the loop's read returns nothing and the skill has no stated fallback for 'no history yet'.
Two shortfalls on superficially-different tickets that are the same 'class' are not recognized as the same class (or vice versa), so the ==2 suppression fires wrongly or never fires.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name (and describe creating) the specific test that asserts neither SKILL.md contains a model/vendor name, e.g. a new tests/unit/test_skill_provider_neutral.py that greps both skill dirs against a vendor/model denylist and exits non-zero on a match.
evidence: AC text: 'Neither skill names a specific model or vendor. Verified by a test.'
Plan grounding names only check_skill_frontmatter.py, test_janitor_concern_schema.py, test_skill_shared_sync.py — none assert vendor/model absence
No described step creates a vendor-neutrality test, so the criterion is an orphan with no covering deliverable
findings.finding: The provider-neutrality acceptance criterion asserts 'Verified by a test' but names no such test, and the plan body/grounding describes no deliverable that creates one — the three named tests (check_skill_frontmatter, test_janitor_concern_schema, test_skill_shared_sync) verify frontmatter/concern-schema/consumer-list, none of them assert the absence of a model or vendor name.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'Neither skill names a specific model or vendor. Verified by a test.'
scenarios: An executor marks the AC done by eyeballing the skill files, with no deterministic command producing evidence
A later edit reintroduces a vendor name and no test catches it
findings.suggested_fix: Add a deliverable and proving command: a test that scans both examples/agent-skills/rebar-tidy/ and rebar-janitor/ SKILL.md (and phase files) for a denylist of vendor/model tokens and fails if any is present; cite it in the AC in place of the bare 'Verified by a test.'

findings.checklist_item: Require the tidying-janitor skill body to enumerate the closed seven-kind mechanism list inline (lock, env_var, config_key, feature_flag, ci_gate, autouse_fixture, test_helper), each with a one-line prose-recognition cue and a statement that the list is closed, and add an AC asserting the skill names all seven as literal strings.
evidence: Plan: 'mechanisms retired by kind and name (the seven kinds the ratchet counts, scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py)' — points at a script path, not inline vocabulary.

scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py:9-11 defines the closed enum: lock, env_var, config_key, feature_flag, ci_gate, autouse_fixture, test_helper (not readable by a prose-time agent summing deltas before any code/diff exists).

Dependency ticket fe94 ('Self-contained taxonomy'): a prose-time reviewer 'runs at claim time against plan prose with no tree access, so it has no runtime source for the taxonomy. The rubric body must ENUMERATE the closed seven-kind list inline ... each with a one-line cue for recognising it in plan prose, and must state the list is closed.' The tidying janitor's declare/sum step is the same no-tree-access situation.

The script computes --check/--update-stale against the committed baseline/live tree; it does NOT compute the mechanism delta of a proposed future deletion, so the agent cannot outsource kind-recognition to it at declaration time.
findings.finding: The tidying janitor must declare 'mechanisms retired by kind and name (the seven kinds the ratchet counts)' and sum declared deltas BEFORE filing at a discovery SHA, but the plan references the seven-kind vocabulary only by script path (scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py) and no contract bullet or AC requires the closed seven-kind list — with a recognition cue per kind — to be enumerated inline in the skill body the agent reads.
findings.location: The change — 'each ticket it files states ... mechanisms retired by kind and name (the seven kinds the ratchet counts, scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py)'; Acceptance criteria lines 'mechanisms retired by kind and name' and 'summed declared delta'
scenarios: An executor writing the tidying-janitor SKILL.md omits the enum, assuming the referenced script supplies it, leaving the agent to invent an open-ended notion of 'mechanism' when declaring per-ticket deltas.
Two runs classify the same deletion under different kinds (or miss ci_gate/autouse_fixture entirely) because no closed list with cues is co-located, making the summed-delta metric non-reproducible.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror fe94's 'Self-contained taxonomy' section in the tidying-janitor skill: list the seven kinds with a recognition cue each, state the list is closed, and add AC: 'The tidying janitor's skill body names all seven mechanism kinds as literal strings.'

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: State how a declared per-ticket delta is substantiated at the discovery SHA before the run sums it (e.g. require the declaration to cite the exact lines/mechanism-sites to be removed so the sum is auditable at file time), so the success metric is not an unchecked self-estimate corrected only one run later.
evidence: Plan: 'the run itself sums those declared deltas before filing, and a run whose sum is not negative files nothing and says so — that sum, not tickets filed, is the run's result'
Plan: 'a closed tidying ticket whose merged diff removed less than it declared records the shortfall' — this is the ONLY correction and it is lagged by a full run

The split KEEPs 'blind verification' but the plan frames verification as the defect audit's floor machinery (validity/impact); it does not state that the tidying janitor independently verifies a declared deletion's achievability at declaration time
ABSENCE: the plan does not name who/what checks, before filing, that a ticket's declared LOC/mechanism removal is realizable at the discovery SHA (vs. the agent's estimate)
findings.finding: The tidying janitor's success metric (summed DECLARED delta computed by the run before filing) is a self-reported prediction by the proposing agent, and the only stated correction is the NEXT run's retrospective shortfall read from closed tickets. No in-run, independent check verifies at the discovery SHA that each declared deletion actually removes the LOC/mechanisms it claims. A run can therefore report a net-negative result, file tickets, and have them merge net-neutral or net-positive, with the gap caught only one run later.
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard: the summed-declared-delta bullet and the corrective-loop bullet; AC 'Its success metric is the summed declared delta ... computed by the run before filing'
scenarios: A proposer declares that removing a feature_flag retires 120 LOC, but the flag has live readers that must be preserved, so the merged diff nets +0; the shortfall surfaces only on the subsequent run
Two different change classes each over-declare by a small amount in one run; the run's summed delta clears the 'negative' bar and files, though the realized merge is non-negative

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the tidying janitor invokes scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py (and which entry point) to count the seven mechanism kinds, or references its taxonomy in prose only, so the measure cannot drift from the ratchet.
evidence: scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py defines KINDS and exposes census/detect_all/evaluate in __all__ (verified)
The plan names the script as the measure source but is prompt-shaped; it does not state whether the run shells out to the script, reuses its API, or just mirrors the taxonomy in prose
findings.finding: The plan references scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py as the authority for the 'seven kinds' a tidying ticket must declare, but does not specify whether the tidying janitor consumes the script programmatically (e.g., its census/detect_all/evaluate API) or only cites its kind taxonomy in prompt prose; the script exists and exposes those symbols, so this is an integration-contract ambiguity rather than a missing target.
findings.location: The change — tidying janitor contract, bullet: 'mechanisms retired by kind and name (the seven kinds the ratchet counts, scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py)'
scenarios: Author or implementer must decide whether the tidying janitor's per-run delta sum is computed by invoking the existing script versus the skill re-deriving the seven kinds by hand, risking a divergent second definition of the measure

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that the tidying janitor states each filed ticket must be landable in one session, or fold it into the cap-of-5 AC.
evidence: Change bullet: 'a run is capped at 5 tickets, each landable in one session'
AC covers only: 'It declares a per-run ticket cap of 5.' — the 'each landable in one session' half has no covering criterion
findings.finding: The change section constrains each filed ticket to be 'landable in one session', but no acceptance criterion covers that per-ticket sizing constraint — only the per-run cap of 5 is given an AC.
findings.location: The change section ('capped at 5 tickets, each landable in one session') vs Acceptance criteria
scenarios: A reviewer confirms the cap-of-5 AC but the skill never states the one-session-per-ticket sizing rule, and oversized tickets ship
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the cap AC to: 'It declares a per-run ticket cap of 5 and states each filed ticket must be landable in one session.'
